issues.claim: R5-02's P8 at §4.8's lead (l. 7610–7612) reads "the strips S7 cuts beside that trace stop at its under-deck strip's edges, their setback, glacis and berm closed along them"; P3 at §4.1's S7 row (l. 4952) "its strips stopped at the under-deck strip"; P12 at §4.13's `wall` cell (l. 9017) "runs on beneath its deck … its strips stopped at the under-deck strip". A wall strip is the band's half plus the setback inside, or the setback and glacis (or the berm) outside (§4.8 *Wall strips* l. 7618–7625; §2.7 (3)'s obstacle "its band's half, setback and glacis"), and S10's step (0) builds the enceinte's half-band only inside the strip blocks S7 cuts, `Enceinte.band` being their union (§4.7 l. 6785–6796). As written no band is built beneath the deck: the curtain is open under every raised way a later wall meets. The canonical home, §2.7's support step (6) (d) (l. 2603–2616), stops only "the stretch's setback, glacis and berm" there and runs the wall on beneath the deck — each support, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span in its band taken into the line, beneath every other span "an ordinary run whose top is no higher than that span's soffit", read by §4.5's casters, §8.4's casters and heightfield and §11.1's glTF wall — and T110-2's lead and (4) bar that run. Two builders of S7: one cuts no strip under the deck (no band, the curtain breached), the other builds the band there. The same sentence of §4.8's lead also omits (6) (d)'s tower rule (no tower in the under-deck strip, one moved along the trace clear of it), which S7's tower spacing must apply, and §4.1's row names only the supports where §4.8 names supports, ramps, stairs and feet and adds breakwaters. The same loose wording stands at §7.3's S7 row (l. 10883, determinism) and V06's W68 (l. 351) and §3.7.1 (l. 1462–1463).
issues.required_change: §4.8's lead l. 7611–7612: "the strips S7 cuts beside that trace stop at its under-deck strip's edges, their setback, glacis and berm closed along them, reported (`W_RAISED_CROSSING`);" → "the strips S7 cuts beside that trace run on beneath its deck as the band's halves only — their setback, glacis and berm stopped at its under-deck strip's edges and closed along them, reported (`W_RAISED_CROSSING`), S10's step (0) building the band there as §2.7's support step (6) (d) lays the run — and no tower stands in the under-deck strip, one the spacing would place there moving along the trace to the nearest point clear of it;". §4.1's S7 row l. 4952: "its strips stopped at the under-deck strip, a gate plaza cut round the raised way's supports and no pier or mole rooted on them" → "its strips' setback, glacis and berm stopped at the under-deck strip (the band running on beneath the deck), a gate plaza cut round the raised way's supports, ramps, stairs and feet and no pier, mole or breakwater rooted on them". §4.13's `wall` cell l. 9017: "its strips stopped at the under-deck strip" → "its setback, glacis and berm stopped at the under-deck strip". END at determinism: §7.3's S7 row l. 10883 "and its strips stopped at the under-deck strip's edges" → "and its setback, glacis and berm stopped at the under-deck strip's edges". END at V06: W68 l. 351 "its strips stopped at the under-deck strip's edges" → "its setback, glacis and berm stopped at the under-deck strip's edges"; §3.7.1 l. 1462–1463 "its strips stopping there" → "its setback, glacis and berm stopping there".

issues.claim: §4.11's `wallToWay` (l. 8214–8221) retypes the wall chain as the ring road's spine "on the same edges", excepting only "the stretch held under a raised way's crossing station while its deck stands …, which stays as a free-standing gate tower or arch carrying the deck, the new ring road taking no junction with the raised way" (VDC4-05's text, this round). Two meetings with a standing raised way have no outcome for the road: (1) that kept stretch stands on the old wall's line, so the road's spine on the same edges runs into the free-standing gate tower or the curtain under the arch (a raised gate's portal is on the raised part only, §4.8 l. 7672–7673); (2) since R5-02 a wall stretch laid after a raised way runs on beneath its deck with each support, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span in its band taken into its line and no crossing station (§2.7 (6) (d)), so the save clause does not reach it and the road's spine passes through those parts — a support standing in a road, or a road through an arch vault's chamber (II.7.6). §2.7 (6) (a) makes every part-0 way laid after a raised way cross its under-deck strip only by §4.3's crossing rule, else end at the strip, but `wallToWay` neither cites nor applies it, nor does V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s bullet ("leave standing every raised way that crosses the old line; the new ring road takes no junction with it"). The path is an ordinary one at growing CITY and METROPOLIS epochs (a superseded ring's `road` end, V06 §3.7.2 (3); case (1) is H-AQUA's own CITY ring under its founded aqueduct, run by T-V6-47; case (2) T110-2's lead fixture once its stage-2 ring is superseded). Two builders: the road through the supports or the kept stretch, or the road re-routed or ended at the strip. Untested: T-V6-47's `wallToWay` clause checks only that the raised way and its station stand.
issues.required_change: §4.11 `wallToWay` l. 8221, after "(§2.7's support step (3); V06 §3.7.6 (5) gives its form).": add "Where the old line meets a standing raised way — at that kept stretch, or where a run laid after the raised way ran on beneath its deck (§2.7's support step (6) (d)) — the ring road is a part-0 way laid after the raised way (§2.7's support step (6) (a)): in the dry run its spine there is re-routed by §7.3's S4 local operator, between its nearest nodes on either side of the under-deck strip, to cross under the nearest span §4.3's crossing rule admits, else it ends at the strip's edges as at a reservation, reported; the kept stretch and every part of the raised way the old run took into its line stand untouched." END at V06: §3.7.6 (5)'s bullet "the new ring road takes **no junction** with it" adds "and crosses its under-deck strip as a way laid after it (§4.11's `wallToWay`)"; T-V6-47's `wallToWay` clause adds "the ring road crossing the aqueduct's under-deck strip under a span §4.3 admits, clear of the kept stretch, else ended at the strip; and, on a fixture this test names, `wallToWay` of a ring laid after a standing viaduct with a support in its band — 0 way corridors over a support ring, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span".
